sources.note: Jawoyn-Warray subgrouping paper. Its one stress remark (p. 288: four-syllable unanalysable roots normatively stressed on 1st and 3rd syllables; prefix + trisyllabic stem gives a single primary stress on the 2nd syllable) concerns WARRAY place names (Anpekkola, Anporrokkorl), not Jawoyn.

sources.citation: Merlan, Francesca. 2016. Tricksters and Traditions: Jawoyn Stories and Story-tellers of southern Arnhemland. Asia-Pacific Linguistics A-PL 31. Canberra: ANU (194 pp., CC-BY 4.0).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: 'Orthography, Spelling and Questions and Notes on Audio Files' (pp. 6-8) gives the segment inventory, positions of the long/short stop contrast, glottal stop and spelling conventions; nothing on stress or accent. Explicitly refers readers to 'the Grammar Outline in the Jawoyn-English Dictionary (Merlan and Jacq 2005a, b)'.

sources.citation: Harvey, Mark. 2003. An initial reconstruction of Proto Gunwinyguan phonology. In N. Evans (ed.), The non-Pama-Nyungan languages of northern Australia, 205-268. Pacific Linguistics 552. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 4.3 'Jawoyn' (pp. 223-224) treats only lenition of medial singleton stops; 'stress' appears only in the Bininj Gun-wok, Dalabon and Rembarrnga sections (changes in unstressed vowels). No statement of Jawoyn stress placement and no general Gunwinyguan stress statement.
